ActState.description:
The current act-state as read from the ledger fold.

The ledger is append-only, so a sealed record is never rewritten:
transitions are appended as [`DecisionAct`] lines and the CURRENT state is
the fold of those lines. Absent on records sealed before act-state existed
— read that as unknown, never as confirmed.

at.description: RFC 3339 — when this state was recorded.

retryable.description:
Whether a `failed` act may be retried (decision coherence §3): the
reconciler retries retryable failures with backoff and PARKS
non-retryable ones for the operator. Absent on non-failed states and
on failures recorded before this field existed — absent reads as
retryable, because the upstream settle is idempotent (cortex#98) and
a wasted retry is recoverable where a silently-parked act is not.

ActStatus.description:
What became of a sealed decision's upstream act (decision coherence §2,
operator requirement 2026-08-21).

"Sealed but not confirmed" is the state that had no name — which is
exactly why nothing could act on it when the settle hop failed: the
ledger held cryptographic proof of a decision and the system behaved as
though none existed. Naming the state is most of the fix.

oneOf.description: Verified and recorded; the act not yet attempted.
Upstream refused or was unreachable; `reason` carries why.

CardContainment.description:
Everything a contained RED card carries so a signer sees, and signs, the
containment the run will get.

containment_sha256.description:
[`Containment::sha256`], computed by reflexd at queue time. The deck
puts it in the signing input as `containment_sha256` and never
computes it itself.

profile.description:
The resolved profile, verbatim from the registry entry — shown to the
signer (tier included), never re-rendered from a second source.

CardDecided.description:
The daemon's own sealed verdict on a card that is nonetheless still
pending upstream (bridge task #54).

Present when the decision ledger holds an ACCEPTED decision for the card
while the source system still lists it — which means the DECISION
happened and only the upstream act is unconfirmed. Rendering such a card
as an open decision is the lie this field exists to prevent: it invited
a second signature over the same payload, and three sealed records where
there was one decision is, after the fact, indistinguishable from an
operator who changed their mind twice.

Deliberately not a filter. A decided-but-unsettled card is a REAL failure
the operator must see (the upstream act did not complete); it must simply
stop being signable.

accepted_decisions.description:
How many ACCEPTED decisions the ledger holds for this card. Anything
above 1 is itself evidence of the defect this field fixes, and is
surfaced rather than collapsed.

act.description:
What became of the act (decision coherence §2) — why a decided card is
still in the source's pending list. Absent = unknown, which the deck
must render as unknown, never as confirmed.

actor_email.description: Who signed it, as verified at seal time.

ts.description: When the (latest) accepted decision was signed.

CardGuard.description: A guard's finding about a card, when the source carries one.

CardSource.description: Which queue a card came from.

oneOf.description: A card in cortex, raised by a lane via `cortex-card`.
A RED-tier action in reflexd's own queue.

Containment.description:
What reflex asks the executor to enforce for one run.

Every field is a string or an array of strings. [`Self::canonical_json`]
is the shared RFC 8785 implementation in [`crate::jcs`] (CER-2276); a
numeric field added here must stay within its integers-only profile, and
changes [`Self::sha256`] for every containment that carries it.

policy.description:
The reflex containment-seed id that chose it, cited like a
classification's policy (`"soma/comms:draft@v1"`).

profile_digest.description:
`"sha256:<lowercase hex>"` — the registry entry's own digest, copied
verbatim from [`ProfileEntry::digest`]. reflex never computes it.

required_layers.description:
The layers the executor must attest, copied in the order the registry
served them. Order is significant to [`Self::sha256`].

containment.description:
The containment a contained RED action will run under, with the
resolved profile to show and the `containment_sha256` to sign
(EST-318, ratified Q2(b)). Computed by reflexd when the card is
queued; the deck passes the hash into the signing input and never
recomputes it. Absent = the action carries no containment.

custody.description:
Where the run record behind this card lives (CANON §1c, EST-185):
`blackwall-serve` (in-cluster — reflexd's settle hop resolves against
it) or `fleet:<agent>` (a runner's own store, which the settle hop
cannot reach). The deck decides signability from this value.

Passed through verbatim from the producer and **never defaulted**:
`None` means the producer did not say, which the deck renders as
"custody not reported" — a different fact from `blackwall-serve`, and
one reflexd must not invent. Session cards carry none by design;
reflex's own RED cards carry none until an executor records one.

decided.description:
See [`CardDecided`]. `None` = the ledger holds no accepted decision
for this card; the card is genuinely open.

id.description:
cortex `job_id`, or a reflex action id. Unique only WITHIN a source —
which is why [`CardSource`] travels with it and why the decision record
names the queue.

payload_hash.description:
The content address of what the agent asked to do, as bare lowercase
hex — the bytes a `reflex-red` decision signs (EST-212; §1c
`reflexd ↔ deck` row). Absent when the source carries none: cortex
cards bind to the title until they have a content address.

Computed once, by reflexd, at submit — the hex after a VERIFIED
`sha256:` label on the action's `payload_hash` (`reflex_binding_hex`);
a card whose action carries any other or absent label gets `None`,
never a guess. The deck passes it through and never recomputes it —
a client-side re-hash would be a second implementation of the
binding (§1c rule 3). Population is EST-214 (reflex lane); until
then the deck reads the same value from the `/v1/queue` join.

title.description: One line for the operator. cortex supplies `changeset.description`.

upstream_settle_url.description:
cortex's own settle URL, carried for provenance and **not** for the deck
to POST to.

Two reasons. It currently points at a cluster-internal address that no
workstation can open — a known defect. And more fundamentally, settling
through it would bypass reflexd, which is where the operator's signed
decision is verified and sealed; a settle path that skips verification
is the thing this whole design exists to remove. The deck settles via
reflexd and reflexd makes the upstream hop.
